correctness.rationale: The first-larger-value argument proves π_1≥n−m; reversal plus complementation gives π_n≤m+1. The closing edge forces n≤3m+1. The explicit five-block word at equality is a permutation, has jumps at most m, and avoids 123. Deleting at most two largest high-block entries covers all lower orders; equality forces the first, second, penultimate and last entries. The finite checker independently cross-compares direct triples with a dynamic count and tests the witness construction, but the unbounded theorem uses the handwritten proof.
